rows.stem: In which one of the following situations a chemical reaction does **not** occur?

options.label: A
options.text: Milk is left open at room temperature during summer

options.label: C
options.text: An iron nail is left exposed to humid atmosphere

rows.solution:
Souring of milk, fermentation of grapes and rusting of iron all form new substances, so each is a chemical change.

Melting of glaciers only changes ice into liquid water: the substance stays water, so it is a physical change and no chemical reaction occurs. This is option (D) Melting of glaciers.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem: In order to prepare dry hydrogen chloride gas in humid atmosphere the gas produced is passed through a guard tube (drying tube) which contains :
rows.solution:
A guard tube must absorb moisture without reacting with hydrogen chloride. Anhydrous calcium chloride is a drying agent and does not react with HCl.

Calcium oxide, calcium hydroxide and calcium carbonate are basic and would react with the acidic gas. The tube contains option (A) Calcium chloride.

rows.subtopic: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-metals
rows.stem: The property by virtue of which a solid material can be drawn into thin wires is called :
rows.solution: The ability of a material to be drawn into thin wires is ductility (malleability is being beaten into thin sheets). This is option (B) ductility.

rows.stem: Select from the following a hydrocarbon having one \(\mathrm{C{-}C}\) bond and one \(\mathrm{C{\equiv}C}\) bond :
rows.solution:
Propyne is \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}C{\equiv}CH}\): one carbon-carbon single bond and one carbon-carbon triple bond.

Benzene and cyclohexane have no triple bond, and butyne (four carbons) has two C-C single bonds besides its triple bond. This is option (D) Propyne.

rows.stem: The essential element taken up from the soil by the plants to synthesize proteins is :
rows.solution: Proteins contain nitrogen, which plants take up from the soil as nitrates and nitrites. This is option (B) Nitrogen.

rows.stem:
Select **TRUE** statements about lymph from the following :

A. Lymph vessels carry lymph through the body and finally open into larger arteries.

B. Lymph contains some amount of plasma, proteins and blood cells.

C. Lymph contains some amount of plasma, proteins and red blood cells.

D. Lymph vessels carry lymph through the body and finally open into larger veins.

**The true statements are :**
rows.solution:
Lymph is formed from plasma, proteins and blood cells that escape into intercellular spaces; it carries some white blood cells but no red blood cells. So statement B is true and C is false.

Lymph vessels drain into the larger veins, not arteries, so D is true and A is false.

The true statements are B and D, which is option (B) B and D.

rows.stem: Plants like rose and banana have lost the capacity to produce :
rows.solution: Plants such as rose and banana are grown by vegetative propagation and have lost the capacity to produce seeds. This is option (C) seeds.

rows.stem: In a bisexual flower the male gametes are present in the :
rows.solution: The male germ cells are produced in the pollen grains, which are formed in the anther of the stamen. This is option (A) anther.

rows.stem: When a pure-tall pea plant is crossed with a pure-dwarf pea plant, the percentage of tall pea plants in \(\mathrm{F_1}\) and \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation pea plants will be respectively :
rows.solution:
Pure tall (TT) crossed with pure dwarf (tt) gives only Tt in \(\mathrm{F_1}\): all tall, 100%.

Selfing \(\mathrm{F_1}\) gives TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1, so three-quarters are tall, 75%.

This is option (C) 100% ; 75%.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem: To get an image of magnification \(-1\) on a screen using a lens of focal length 20 cm, the object distance must be :
rows.solution:
A magnification of \(-1\) means a real, inverted image of the same size. A convex lens forms this when the object is at 2F, that is, at twice the focal length: \(2 \times 20 = 40\) cm.

This is option (C) 40 cm.

rows.stem: An optical device ‘X’ is placed obliquely in the path of a narrow parallel beam of light. If the emergent beam gets displaced laterally, the device ‘X’ is :
rows.solution:
A rectangular glass slab placed obliquely in a beam makes the emergent beam parallel to the incident beam but shifted sideways (lateral displacement). A prism deviates the beam, and a mirror or lens changes its direction.

The device is option (C) glass slab.

rows.stem: A piece of wire of resistance ‘R’ is cut lengthwise into three identical parts. These parts are then connected in parallel. If the equivalent resistance of this combination is \(R'\), then the value of \(R/R'\) is :
rows.solution:
Each third has resistance \(\dfrac{R}{3}\). Three equal resistors in parallel give \(R' = \dfrac{R/3}{3} = \dfrac{R}{9}\).

So \(\dfrac{R}{R'} = 9\), which is option (D) 9.

rows.stem: An electric bulb is rated 220 V; 11W. The resistance of its filament when it glows with a power supply of 220 V is :
rows.solution: \(P = \dfrac{V^2}{R}\), so \(R = \dfrac{V^2}{P} = \dfrac{220 \times 220}{11} = 4400\,\Omega\). This is option (A) \(4400\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: The minimum number of identical bulbs of rating 4V; 6W, that can work safely with desired brightness, when connected in series with a 240 V mains supply is :
rows.solution:
Each bulb works properly with 4 V across it. In series the supply voltage is shared equally, so the number of bulbs is \(\dfrac{240}{4} = 60\).

This is option (C) 60.

rows.stem: In the food chains given below. Select the most efficient food chain in terms of energy :

options.label: D
options.text: Phytoplankton \(\rightarrow\) Zooplankton \(\rightarrow\) Small Fish \(\rightarrow\) Big Fish

rows.solution:
Only about 10% of the energy passes from one trophic level to the next, so the shortest chain loses the least energy. Plants to man has only two levels.

This is option (C) Plants \(\rightarrow\) Man.

rows.stem: Which one of the following gets biomagnified at different levels in a food chain ?
rows.solution: DDT is a non-biodegradable pesticide that accumulates in organisms and its concentration increases at each higher trophic level. This is option (C) DDT.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** In large animals, oxygen can reach different parts of the animal’s body easily.

**Reason (R) :** Respiratory pigments take up oxygen from the air and carry it to body tissues.
rows.context: Question Nos. 17 to 20 consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
In large animals diffusion alone is too slow to supply oxygen to all parts of the body, so the Assertion is false.

Respiratory pigments such as haemoglobin do take up oxygen and carry it to the tissues, so the Reason is true.

So the Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Concentrated nitric acid is diluted by adding water slowly to acid with constant stirring.

**Reason (R) :** Concentrated nitric acid is easily soluble in water.
rows.context: Question Nos. 17 to 20 consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
A concentrated acid must be diluted by adding the acid slowly to water with constant stirring, never water to the acid; the heat released could make the mixture splash. So the Assertion is false.

Concentrated nitric acid does dissolve readily in water, so the Reason is true.

This is option (D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** In reptiles, the temperature at which the fertilized eggs are kept decides the sex of the offsprings.

**Reason (R) :** Sex is not genetically determined in some animals.
rows.context: Question Nos. 17 to 20 consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
In some reptiles the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept decides whether the offspring are male or female, so the Assertion is true.

This happens because in such animals sex is not determined genetically, which is the Reason. It is true and explains the Assertion.

This is option (A) Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** When ciliary muscles contract, eye lens becomes thin.

**Reason (R) :** Ciliary muscles control the power of the eye lens.
rows.context: Question Nos. 17 to 20 consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option (a), (b), (c) and (d) as given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both, Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is **not** the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
When the ciliary muscles contract, the eye lens becomes thicker (its focal length decreases, for near vision). So the Assertion, which says it becomes thin, is false.

The ciliary muscles do change the curvature and hence the power of the lens, so the Reason is true.

This is option (D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.stem:
Define oxidation. Identify and name the substance oxidised in the following reaction :

\(\mathrm{CuO + H_2 \rightarrow Cu + H_2O}\)
rows.solution:
Oxidation is the gain of oxygen by a substance, or the loss of hydrogen from it (or the loss of electrons).

In \(\mathrm{CuO + H_2 \rightarrow Cu + H_2O}\), hydrogen gains oxygen to form water, so the substance oxidised is hydrogen, \(\mathrm{H_2}\).

rows.stem: Show the formation of magnesium chloride by electron transfer. Write the name of the cation and anion present in the compound formed. (Atomic Number of Mg = 12, Cl = 17)
rows.solution:
Magnesium (2, 8, 2) loses its two valence electrons, one to each of two chlorine atoms (2, 8, 7):

\(\mathrm{Mg \rightarrow Mg^{2+} + 2e^-}\) and \(\mathrm{2Cl + 2e^- \rightarrow 2Cl^-}\), giving \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}(Cl^-)_2}\), that is, \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\).

In the electron-dot drawing, the two dots of magnesium are shown moving by arrows, one to each chlorine atom, which then carries a complete octet in brackets with a single negative charge.

The cation is the magnesium ion, \(\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}\), and the anion is the chloride ion, \(\mathrm{Cl^-}\).

rows.stem: How is zinc extracted from its ore? Name the processes involved in the extraction and write chemical equations for the reactions that occur during these processes.
rows.solution:
Zinc is in the middle of the reactivity series. Its ore is first converted to the oxide, which is then reduced with carbon.

If the ore is a sulphide (zinc blende), it is roasted, that is, heated strongly in excess air:

\(\mathrm{2ZnS + 3O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2ZnO + 2SO_2}\)

If the ore is a carbonate (calamine), it is calcined, that is, heated strongly in limited air:

\(\mathrm{ZnCO_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} ZnO + CO_2}\)

The zinc oxide is then reduced by heating with carbon:

\(\mathrm{ZnO + C \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Zn + CO}\)

So the processes are roasting (or calcination) followed by reduction.

rows.stem: “Plants use a variety of techniques to get rid of waste material.” Justify this statement giving any four ways.
rows.solution:
Plants get rid of waste in several ways (any four):

1. Oxygen produced in photosynthesis is released as a waste product through the stomata.

2. Excess water is removed by transpiration.

3. Many wastes are stored in leaves, which then fall off (shedding of leaves).

4. Some wastes are stored as resins and gums, especially in old xylem.

5. Some waste substances are excreted into the soil around the roots.

6. Some wastes are stored in the cellular vacuoles.

rows.stem: Explain with the help of a flow chart that in human beings father is responsible for the sex (male or female) of the child.
rows.solution:
A woman has two X chromosomes (XX), so all her eggs carry an X chromosome. A man has one X and one Y chromosome (XY), so half his sperms carry X and half carry Y.

Flow chart:

Mother (XX) gives eggs: X, X. Father (XY) gives sperms: X, Y.

Egg X + sperm X gives zygote XX, a girl.

Egg X + sperm Y gives zygote XY, a boy.

Since the mother always contributes an X, the sex of the child depends on whether the father's sperm carries X or Y. So the father determines the sex of the child.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Draw a ray diagram to show the refraction of a ray of light passing through an equilateral glass prism. Mark the angle through which the emergent ray bends from the direction of the incident ray and also name it.
rows.solution:
Draw an equilateral triangle ABC as the prism. Let a ray (the incident ray) strike face AB obliquely. At AB it bends towards the normal and travels through the glass to face AC, where it bends away from the normal and leaves as the emergent ray.

Extend the incident ray forwards and the emergent ray backwards so that they meet. The angle between them is the angle through which the light has bent; it is called the angle of deviation.

(The marking scheme gives one mark for the diagram and half a mark for labelling.)

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: Name the type of lenses required by the persons for the correction of their defect of vision called presbyopia. Write the structure of the lenses commonly used for the correction of this defect giving reason for such designs.
rows.solution:
Presbyopia is corrected with bifocal lenses.

A common bifocal lens has a concave lens in its upper portion and a convex lens in its lower portion. The upper part helps distant vision (for those who also have myopia) and the lower part helps near vision, for reading. People who need only near correction can use a convex lens, which is thicker at the middle than at the edges.

rows.stem: What are magnetic field lines. List two important properties of magnetic field lines.
rows.solution:
Magnetic field lines are the lines that represent the magnetic field around a magnet: the direction of the field at any point is the direction of the tangent to the line, and the path a north pole would tend to follow.

Two properties (any two):

1. No two field lines cross each other.

2. Outside the magnet they emerge from the north pole and merge at the south pole; inside the magnet they run from the south pole to the north pole, so they are closed curves.

3. The lines are closer together where the field is stronger.

rows.stem:
Why do we balance a chemical equation? Name and state the law that suggests the balancing of a chemical equation? Balance the following chemical equation :

\(\mathrm{Zn + H_3PO_4 \rightarrow Zn_3(PO_4)_2 + H_2}\)
rows.solution:
A chemical equation is balanced so that the number of atoms of each element is the same on both sides, because atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a reaction.

This follows the law of conservation of mass: mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

Balanced equation:

\(\mathrm{3Zn + 2H_3PO_4 \rightarrow Zn_3(PO_4)_2 + 3H_2}\)

rows.stem: Define a precipitation reaction. Give its example and also express the reaction that occurs in the form of a balanced chemical equation.
rows.solution:
A precipitation reaction is a reaction in which an insoluble substance (a precipitate) is formed.

Example: when sodium sulphate solution is added to barium chloride solution, a white precipitate of barium sulphate forms:

\(\mathrm{Na_2SO_4(aq) + BaCl_2(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s) + 2NaCl(aq)}\)

rows.subtopic: Physical Properties of Metals and Non-metals
rows.stem: Design an activity to show that metals are good conductors of heat and have high melting points.
rows.solution:
Activity: clamp an aluminium or copper wire on a stand. Fix a pin to the free end of the wire with a little wax. Heat the wire with a spirit lamp or burner near the place where it is clamped.

Observation: after some time the wax melts and the pin falls off, but the wire itself does not melt.

Conclusion: heat travelled along the metal to its far end, so metals are good conductors of heat; and the wire did not melt in the flame, so metals have high melting points.

rows.stem:
The digestion of food in human alimentary canal is a complex process. State the enzyme/salt present in the following and mention their function in the process of digestion :

(i) Saliva

(ii) Bile Juice

(iii) Pancreatic Juice
rows.solution:
(i) Saliva contains the enzyme salivary amylase, which breaks down starch into simple sugar.

(ii) Bile juice contains bile salts, which make the acidic food from the stomach alkaline and break large fat globules into smaller ones (emulsification).

(iii) Pancreatic juice contains trypsin, which digests proteins, and lipase, which breaks down emulsified fats.

rows.stem: State two limitations of electrical impulses in multicellular organisms. Why is chemical communication better than electrical impulses as a means of communication between cells in multicellular organisms?
rows.solution:
Limitations of electrical impulses:

1. They reach only those cells that are connected by nervous tissue, not every cell in the body.

2. Once an impulse is generated and transmitted, a cell takes some time to reset its mechanism before it can generate and transmit a new impulse.

Chemical communication is better because the chemical signals (hormones) can reach all cells of the body, steadily and persistently, and bring about the desired changes.

rows.stem: If we want to obtain a virtual and magnified image of an object by using a concave mirror of focal length 18 cm, where should the object be placed? Use mirror formula to determine the object distance for an image of magnification +2 produced by this mirror to justify your answer.
rows.solution:
A concave mirror forms a virtual, magnified image only when the object is between the pole P and the focus F, that is, less than 18 cm from the mirror.

Check with the mirror formula, taking \(f = -18\) cm and \(m = +2\):

\(m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = 2\), so \(v = -2u\).

\(\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\): \(-\dfrac{1}{2u} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{2u} = -\dfrac{1}{18}\), so \(u = -9\) cm.

The object is 9 cm in front of the mirror, which is indeed between P and F.

rows.stem:
The electrical resistivity of three materials A, B and C at 20°C is given below :

| Material | Resistivity (\(\Omega\) m) |
|---|---|
| A | \(10^{17}\) |
| B | \(44 \times 10^{-6}\) |
| C | \(1.62 \times 10^{-8}\) |

(i) Classify these materials as conductor, alloy and insulator.

(ii) Give one example of each of these materials and state one use of each material in the design of an electrical appliance say an electric stove or an electric iron.
rows.solution:
(i) A has a very high resistivity (\(10^{17}\,\Omega\) m), so it is an insulator. C has a very low resistivity (\(1.62 \times 10^{-8}\,\Omega\) m), so it is a conductor. B lies between them, as an alloy's resistivity does, so B is an alloy.

(ii) For example, in an electric iron:

A (insulator): plastic, used for the handle.

B (alloy): nichrome, used for the heating element.

C (conductor): copper, used for the connecting wires.

(In an electric stove: rubber for the feet, nichrome for the heating element, copper for the wires.)

rows.stem: What are decomposers? Give two examples. State how they maintain a balance in an ecosystem.
rows.solution:
Decomposers are micro-organisms that break down the complex organic substances in dead plants and animals into simple inorganic substances. Examples: bacteria and fungi.

The simple substances they release go into the soil and are used again by plants. So nutrients are recycled and the balance of the ecosystem is maintained.

rows.stem: A carbon compound ‘A’ on heating with excess conc. \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) forms a compound ‘B’, which on addition of one mole of hydrogen gas in the presence of nickel catalyst forms a compound ‘C’. ‘C’ on combustion in air forms 2 moles of carbon dioxide and 3 moles of water. Identify ‘A’, ‘B’ and ‘C’ and write their structures. Give chemical equations of the reactions involved. Also state the role of concentrated sulphuric acid in the formation of ‘B’ from ‘A’.
rows.solution:
C burns to give 2 moles of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and 3 moles of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), so it has 2 carbons and 6 hydrogens: C is ethane, \(\mathrm{C_2H_6}\). Ethane comes from adding hydrogen to B, so B is ethene, \(\mathrm{C_2H_4}\), and ethene comes from heating A with excess concentrated sulphuric acid, so A is ethanol, \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}\).

Structures: ethanol \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}OH}\); ethene \(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2}\); ethane \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_3}\) (drawn with all the hydrogen atoms shown).

Reactions:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. } H_2SO_4} CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2O}\)

\(\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni}} CH_3{-}CH_3}\)

\(\mathrm{2C_2H_6 + 7O_2 \rightarrow 4CO_2 + 6H_2O}\) (that is, per mole: \(\mathrm{C_2H_6 + \tfrac{7}{2}O_2 \rightarrow 2CO_2 + 3H_2O}\))

Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent: it removes water from ethanol.

rows.stem:
A carbon compound ‘A’ is widely used as a preservative in pickles and has a molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_4O_2}\). This compound reacts with ethanol to form a sweet smelling compound ‘B’.

(i) Identify the compound ‘A’ and write its structure.

(ii) Write the chemical equation for the reaction of ‘A’ with ethanol to form compound ‘B’. State the role of presence of an acid in the reaction.

(iii) How can we get compound ‘A’ back from ‘B’ ?

(iv) How can ‘A’ be obtained from ethanol ?

(v) Name the gas produced when compound ‘A’ reacts with washing soda.
rows.solution:
(i) A is ethanoic acid (acetic acid), \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\); vinegar, a dilute solution of it, is used as a preservative. Structure: \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}C({=}O){-}OH}\).

(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\)

The product B is ethyl ethanoate, a sweet-smelling ester. The acid acts as a catalyst.

(iii) The ester is heated with dilute sodium hydroxide (saponification), which gives ethanol and sodium ethanoate; acidifying the sodium ethanoate gives back ethanoic acid. (Hydrolysis with water in the presence of an acid also gives back the acid.)

(iv) By oxidising ethanol with alkaline potassium permanganate, or acidified potassium dichromate, on heating:

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{alkaline } KMnO_4 + \text{heat}} CH_3COOH}\)

(v) Carbon dioxide, \(\mathrm{CO_2}\).

rows.stem:
(i) What is regeneration? Give one example of an organism that shows this process and one organism that does not. Why does regeneration not occur in the latter?

(ii) Water in a pond appears dark green and contains filamentous structures. Name these structures and the method by which they reproduce. Explain the process.
rows.solution:
(i) Regeneration is the ability of an organism to give rise to new individual organisms from its body parts: if the organism is cut into pieces, each piece grows into a new organism.

Planaria (or Hydra) shows regeneration. Spirogyra does not.

Regeneration does not occur in Spirogyra because it does not have specialised cells that can multiply and make new cell types and tissues.

(ii) The filamentous structures are Spirogyra, a green alga. It reproduces by fragmentation: on maturing, the filament simply breaks up into smaller pieces, and each piece grows into a new individual.

rows.stem:
(i) Name the part performing following functions in human male reproductive system :

(a) Carries sperm

(b) Production of male gametes

(c) Whose secretion makes the transport of sperms easier

(d) Provide suitable temperature for sperm formation

(ii) Write any two characteristics of sperms.

(iii) What are surgical contraceptive methods? Give the side effect caused by this procedure.
rows.solution:
(i) (a) Vas deferens carries sperms.

(b) The testes produce the male gametes.

(c) The secretions of the prostate gland and seminal vesicles make the transport of sperms easier.

(d) The scrotum keeps the testes at a temperature slightly lower than body temperature, suitable for sperm formation.

(ii) Any two: sperms carry the genetic material; they have a long tail for movement; they are very small in size.

(iii) In surgical methods of contraception, the vas deferens in males (vasectomy) or the fallopian tube in females (tubectomy) is blocked or cut, so that sperms or eggs cannot pass and fertilisation is prevented.

Side effect: if the surgery is not performed properly, it can cause infection and other problems.

rows.stem:
(i) Draw the pattern of the magnetic field lines for the two parallel straight conductors carrying current of same magnitude ‘I’ in opposite directions as shown. Show the direction of magnetic field at a point O which is equidistant from the two conductors. (Consider that the conductors are inserted normal to the plane of a rectangular cardboard.)

(ii) In our houses we receive A.C. electric power of 220 V. In electric iron or electric heater cables having three wires with insulation of three different colours – red, black and green are used to draw current from the mains.

(a) What are these three different wires called? Name them colourwise.

(b) What is the potential difference between the red wire and the black wire?

(c) What is the role of the wire with green insulation in case of accidental leakage of electric current to the metallic body of an electrical appliance?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (i) the two parallel straight conductors, each labelled I with an arrowhead, and the point O midway between them are given only as a drawing; the sense of each current (which one points up) decides the field direction at O and is withheld here. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
(i) Around each straight conductor the field lines are concentric circles centred on the conductor. Their direction is given by the right-hand thumb rule, so the circles round the two conductors run in opposite senses, because the currents are opposite.

At the point O midway between the conductors, the fields due to the two currents point in the same direction, so they add up: the field at O is stronger than that of either conductor alone, and its direction follows from applying the right-hand thumb rule to either conductor at O.

(ii) (a) Red insulation: the live wire. Black insulation: the neutral wire. Green insulation: the earth wire.

(b) The potential difference between the live (red) and neutral (black) wires is 220 V.

(c) The earth wire is a safety measure. If current leaks to the metallic body of an appliance, the earth wire carries it to the earth and keeps the body at the potential of the earth, so the user does not get a severe electric shock.

rows.stem:
(i) By using the given experimental set-up. How can it be shown that :

(a) a force is exerted on the current-carrying conductor AB when it is placed in a magnetic field.

(b) the direction of force can be reversed in two ways.

(ii) When will the magnitude of the force be highest?

(iii) State Fleming’s left hand rule.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the experimental set-up (a conductor AB hung from a stand between the poles of a horseshoe magnet, with a battery and key K in the circuit) is given only as a drawing, and the stem refers to it as 'the given experimental set-up'; the current sense and pole positions are withheld here. Page idx 20.
rows.solution:
(i) (a) When the key is closed and current flows through the conductor AB placed between the poles of the magnet, the conductor AB is displaced (it moves). This shows that a force acts on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

(b) The direction of the force is reversed, and AB moves the other way, if either the direction of the current is reversed or the direction of the magnetic field is reversed (by interchanging the poles of the magnet).

(ii) The force is greatest when the direction of the current is at right angles to the direction of the magnetic field.

(iii) Fleming's left-hand rule: stretch the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand so that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of the magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of the current, then the thumb points in the direction of the force on the conductor.

rows.stem: Name the acid and the base from which common salt can be obtained.
rows.context: Common salt is a very important chemical compound for our daily life. It’s chemical name is sodium chloride and it is used as a raw material in the manufacture of caustic soda, washing soda, baking soda etc. It is also used in the preservation of pickles, butter, meat etc.
rows.solution:
Common salt, sodium chloride, is obtained from hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH):

\(\mathrm{HCl + NaOH \rightarrow NaCl + H_2O}\)

rows.stem: State the nature (acidic/basic/neutral) of sodium chloride. Give reason for the justification for your answer.
rows.context: Common salt is a very important chemical compound for our daily life. It’s chemical name is sodium chloride and it is used as a raw material in the manufacture of caustic soda, washing soda, baking soda etc. It is also used in the preservation of pickles, butter, meat etc.
rows.solution: Sodium chloride is neutral, because it is the salt of a strong acid (hydrochloric acid) and a strong base (sodium hydroxide).

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: What happens when electric current is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (called brine)? Name the products obtained along with the corresponding places in the electrolytic cell where each of these products is obtained.
rows.context: Common salt is a very important chemical compound for our daily life. It’s chemical name is sodium chloride and it is used as a raw material in the manufacture of caustic soda, washing soda, baking soda etc. It is also used in the preservation of pickles, butter, meat etc.
rows.solution:
Passing electricity through brine decomposes it (the chlor-alkali process):

\(\mathrm{2NaCl(aq) + 2H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2NaOH(aq) + Cl_2(g) + H_2(g)}\)

Chlorine gas is given off at the anode, hydrogen gas at the cathode, and sodium hydroxide solution forms near the cathode.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: How is washing soda obtained from sodium chloride? Give chemical equation of the reactions involved in the process.
rows.context: Common salt is a very important chemical compound for our daily life. It’s chemical name is sodium chloride and it is used as a raw material in the manufacture of caustic soda, washing soda, baking soda etc. It is also used in the preservation of pickles, butter, meat etc.
rows.solution:
Sodium chloride is first converted to sodium hydrogencarbonate, which on heating gives sodium carbonate; recrystallising this gives washing soda:

\(\mathrm{NaCl + H_2O + CO_2 + NH_3 \rightarrow NH_4Cl + NaHCO_3}\)

\(\mathrm{2NaHCO_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Na_2CO_3 + H_2O + CO_2}\)

\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 + 10H_2O \rightarrow Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\) (washing soda)

rows.stem: Name the action by which we protect ourself in the situation mentioned above and define it.
rows.context: In life there are certain changes in the environment called ‘stimuli’ to which we respond appropriately. Touching a flame suddenly is a dangerous situation for us. One way is to think consciously about the possibility of burning and then moving the hand. But our body has been designed in such a way that we save ourself from such situations immediately.
rows.solution: Reflex action: a sudden action in response to a stimulus in the environment, made without conscious thought (such as pulling the hand away from a flame).

rows.stem: Write the role of (a) motor and (b) relay neuron.
rows.context: In life there are certain changes in the environment called ‘stimuli’ to which we respond appropriately. Touching a flame suddenly is a dangerous situation for us. One way is to think consciously about the possibility of burning and then moving the hand. But our body has been designed in such a way that we save ourself from such situations immediately.
rows.solution:
(a) A motor neuron carries the message from the spinal cord (or brain) to the effector, the muscle or gland that responds.

(b) A relay neuron, in the spinal cord, connects the sensory neuron to the motor neuron.

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem: What are the two types of nervous system in human body? Name the components of each of them.
rows.context: In life there are certain changes in the environment called ‘stimuli’ to which we respond appropriately. Touching a flame suddenly is a dangerous situation for us. One way is to think consciously about the possibility of burning and then moving the hand. But our body has been designed in such a way that we save ourself from such situations immediately.
rows.solution:
The two types are:

1. The central nervous system, made up of the brain and the spinal cord.

2. The peripheral nervous system, made up of the cranial nerves (arising from the brain) and the spinal nerves (arising from the spinal cord).

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem:
Which part of the human brain is responsible for :

(a) thinking

(b) picking up a pencil

(c) controlling blood pressure

(d) controlling hunger
rows.context: In life there are certain changes in the environment called ‘stimuli’ to which we respond appropriately. Touching a flame suddenly is a dangerous situation for us. One way is to think consciously about the possibility of burning and then moving the hand. But our body has been designed in such a way that we save ourself from such situations immediately.
rows.solution:
(a) Thinking: the fore-brain (cerebrum).

(b) Picking up a pencil (precision of voluntary actions): the cerebellum, in the hind-brain.

(c) Controlling blood pressure: the medulla, in the hind-brain.

(d) Controlling hunger: the fore-brain.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: Give any one more instance in which this type of spectrum is observed.
rows.context: The students in a class took a thick sheet of cardboard and made a small hole in its centre. Sunlight was allowed to fall on this small hole and they obtained a narrow beam of white light. A glass prism was taken and this white light was allowed to fall on one of its faces. The prism was turned slowly until the light that comes out of the opposite face of the prism appeared on the nearby screen. They studied this beautiful band of light and concluded that it is a spectrum of white light.
rows.solution: Any one: a rainbow seen in the sky after rain (or the spectrum seen in a fountain or water spray in sunlight).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: What happens to white light in the above case?
rows.context: The students in a class took a thick sheet of cardboard and made a small hole in its centre. Sunlight was allowed to fall on this small hole and they obtained a narrow beam of white light. A glass prism was taken and this white light was allowed to fall on one of its faces. The prism was turned slowly until the light that comes out of the opposite face of the prism appeared on the nearby screen. They studied this beautiful band of light and concluded that it is a spectrum of white light.
rows.solution: The white light splits into its component colours, from violet to red, because the glass bends light of different colours by different amounts. This splitting is called dispersion of white light.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: List two conditions necessary to observe a rainbow.
rows.context: The students in a class took a thick sheet of cardboard and made a small hole in its centre. Sunlight was allowed to fall on this small hole and they obtained a narrow beam of white light. A glass prism was taken and this white light was allowed to fall on one of its faces. The prism was turned slowly until the light that comes out of the opposite face of the prism appeared on the nearby screen. They studied this beautiful band of light and concluded that it is a spectrum of white light.
rows.solution:
1. There must be water droplets in the atmosphere (after a shower of rain).

2. The sun must be behind the observer.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
Draw a ray diagram to show the formation of a rainbow. Mark on it, points (a), (b) and (c) as given below :

(a) Where dispersion of light occurs.

(b) Where light gets reflected internally.

(c) Where final refraction occurs.
rows.context: The students in a class took a thick sheet of cardboard and made a small hole in its centre. Sunlight was allowed to fall on this small hole and they obtained a narrow beam of white light. A glass prism was taken and this white light was allowed to fall on one of its faces. The prism was turned slowly until the light that comes out of the opposite face of the prism appeared on the nearby screen. They studied this beautiful band of light and concluded that it is a spectrum of white light.
rows.solution:
Draw a spherical raindrop with a ray of sunlight entering it. At the point of entry the light refracts and splits into colours (a: dispersion). At the back surface of the drop the light is reflected internally (b: internal reflection). Where the light leaves the drop it is refracted again (c: final refraction), and the colours come out spread apart towards the observer.

(The marking scheme gives half a mark for the diagram and half a mark for labelling each of a, b and c.)
